items.title: Irreducible representations separate arbitrary C star algebras
items.statement: Assume AC. For every C*-algebra A, with no separability or unit hypothesis, and every nonzero x in A, there is a nonzero irreducible nondegenerate star-representation sigma of A such that sigma(x) is nonzero. Consequently the intersection of the kernels of all irreducible nondegenerate star-representations of A is zero.
items.strategy:
This is a general local supplier, not an import of the separable/Polish lemma on the earlier direct-integral page. Work in the unital algebra D=A if A is unital, otherwise its declared minimal C*-unitization. For a=x*x!=0, the maximal spectral value ||a|| defines a character of C*(I,a), by commutative Gelfand theory. Complex Hahn-Banach extends it to F on D with ||F||=F(I)=1 and F(a)=||a||. Prove positivity explicitly: for selfadjoint c and signed real t, |1+i t F(c)|²<=||I+i t c||²<=1+t²||c||² forces Im F(c)=0. For 0<=c<=I, |1-F(c)|<=||I-c||<=1 forces F(c)>=0. Scaling proves positivity for every positive c. The normalized state space is weak-star compact by Banach-Alaoglu, since positivity and value at I are weak-star closed conditions. Its nonempty norm-attaining face K={phi:phi(a)=||a||} is compact convex: every state has 0<=phi(a)<=||a||, so any convex decomposition of a member of K has both components in K. Weak-star topology is locally convex Hausdorff; the declared Krein-Milman theorem yields an extreme point of K, which is therefore a pure state of D.
Supply the basic unital GNS construction here: Cauchy-Schwarz for the positive form phi(b*a) follows by expanding phi((a+tb)*(a+tb))>=0 and minimizing in complex t. Quotient D by its null vectors, complete under <[a],[b]>=phi(b*a), and define sigma(c)[a]=[ca]. The order inequality a*c*ca<=||c||²a*a proves boundedness with ||sigma(c)||<=||c||, and the product/star identities give a unital star-representation. The class xi=[I] is cyclic and phi(c)=<sigma(c)xi,xi>. To prove irreducibility without a separability assumption, if the representation is reducible, a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace is reducing because sigma(D) is star-closed; the declared Hilbert orthogonal-decomposition and projection suppliers supplies its nontrivial reducing projection E, which commutes with sigma(D). Cyclicity implies t=||E xi||² lies strictly between0 and1. The two normalized vector functionals of E xi and (I-E)xi are states with phi=t phi_1+(1-t)phi_2. Purity forces phi_1=phi_2=phi. Thus for all b,c in D, commutation yields <E sigma(b)xi,sigma(c)xi>=t phi(c*b)=<t sigma(b)xi,sigma(c)xi>. Cyclic density implies E=t I, contradicting E being a projection with0<t<1. So sigma is irreducible, and ||sigma(x)xi||²=phi(x*x)=||x||²>0.
If A is nonunital, it is an ideal in D. The closed subspace H_0=closure sigma(A)H is reducing for sigma(D), nonzero since sigma(x)!=0, hence all H by irreducibility. Thus sigma restricted to A is nondegenerate. Any A-invariant closed subspace reduces sigma(A), and also sigma(D)=sigma(A)+C I, so the restriction remains irreducible. This avoids any unproved pure-state restriction theorem. Applied to each nonzero x, it proves kernel separation. The zero algebra has the empty intersection convention A={0}. No Polish space, countable dense family, sequential approximate identity, or countable group hypothesis is used. AC supplies the Countable Choice hypothesis of the Hilbert projection prerequisites by the declared implication lemma.

items.title: Almost invariant vectors for a unitary representation
items.statement: Let $G$ be a topological group and let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) on a Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]). For a subset $Q\subseteq G$ and a real number $\varepsilon>0$, a vector $\xi\in H$ is **$(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant** if $$\|\pi(x)\xi-\xi\|<\varepsilon\|\xi\|\qquad\text{for every }x\in Q.$$ The condition is vacuous when $Q=\varnothing$; the definition of almost invariant vectors below still tests the compact singleton containing the identity. For $Q=\{e\}$, every unit vector is $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant because $\pi(e)=I$. The representation $\pi$ **has almost invariant vectors** if for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ ([[def-compact-space]]) and every $\varepsilon>0$, it has a $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant unit vector. The representation has a **nonzero invariant vector** if there is $\xi\ne0$ such that $\pi(g)\xi=\xi$ for every $g\in G$. In particular, the zero representation has no almost invariant vectors because it has no unit vectors. For a nonzero $\xi$, the $(Q,\varepsilon)$-condition is unchanged by multiplying $\xi$ by a nonzero scalar, so it may be normalized to a unit vector. For any topological group, almost invariant vectors imply $1_G\prec\pi$ in the finite-sum coefficient sense of [[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]]. Indeed, every coefficient of the trivial representation is a nonnegative constant $c$. If $c>0$, choose a unit vector $\xi$ that is $(Q,\delta)$-invariant, where $\delta=\eta/c$ for a requested approximation tolerance $\eta>0$, and use $\sqrt c\,\xi$ as a vector for $\pi$. For every $x\in Q$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $$\left|c-\langle\pi(x)(\sqrt c\,\xi),\sqrt c\,\xi\rangle\right|=c\left|\langle\xi-\pi(x)\xi,\xi\rangle\right|\le c\|\pi(x)\xi-\xi\|<\eta.$$ This diagonal coefficient is continuous and of positive type by [[def-matrix-coefficient-of-a-unitary-representation]] and [[lem-diagonal-unitary-coefficients-have-positive-type]], so it is an allowed one-term approximant; the zero coefficient ($c=0$) is represented by the zero vector. No choice is used, since a witness is selected separately for each given compact set and tolerance. When $G$ is locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]) and AC is assumed ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), [[lem-weak-containment-of-the-trivial-representation-and-almost-invariant-vectors]] proves the converse as well: $1_G\prec\pi$ is equivalent to almost invariant vectors. Under AC, the converse fails for general topological groups; that published lemma gives a counterexample in its final remarks, using Tychonoff and recursive compact-stage neighbourhood selections. The LCH equivalence and that counterexample are the two assertions invoked here under AC; the definition and the forward implication above are choice-free.
items.strategy: Definition with explicit empty-set, identity-singleton, and zero-representation cases. Nonzero scalar rescaling preserves the (Q,epsilon)-condition. The implication from almost invariant vectors to weak containment follows choice-free from the diagonal coefficient estimate and Cauchy-Schwarz, with the zero coefficient handled by the zero vector. The converse is cited only for LCH groups under the published lemma's AC hypothesis; its final remark supplies a counterexample outside that scope under AC, with a complete local compact-stage product argument.

items.title: Kazhdan pairs, Kazhdan sets and Kazhdan constants
items.statement: Let G be a topological group. For Q⊆G and ε>0, (Q,ε) is a Kazhdan pair for G if every strongly continuous unitary representation of G having a (Q,ε)-invariant unit vector has a nonzero G-invariant vector. A subset Q⊆G is a Kazhdan set if (Q,ε) is a Kazhdan pair for some ε>0. For any Q⊆G and unitary representation π on a Hilbert space H, define d_Q(π,ξ)=0 if Q=∅ and d_Q(π,ξ)=sup_{x∈Q}||π(x)ξ−ξ|| otherwise, for ||ξ||=1. Define κ(G,Q,π)=inf_{||ξ||=1}d_Q(π,ξ) in the extended real line, with inf∅=+∞; it lies in [0,2] when H≠{0} and equals +∞ when H={0}. Define κ(G,Q)=sup_{ ar R}({0}∪{ε>0:(Q,ε) is a Kazhdan pair}). A Kazhdan pair implies κ(G,Q)≥ε, every 0<ε<κ(G,Q) is a Kazhdan parameter, and each π without nonzero invariant vectors satisfies κ(G,Q,π)≥κ(G,Q). If Q is compact, then (Q,ε) is a Kazhdan pair iff κ(G,Q)≥ε, and κ(G,Q)=inf_π κ(G,Q,π), where the infimum is over unitary representations without nonzero invariant vectors, including the zero-space representation with value +∞. For noncompact Q, no endpoint equivalence is asserted.
items.strategy: Definition plus monotonicity, displacement bounds, and compact attainment for the endpoint equivalence; arbitrary-Q endpoint is treated with a strict threshold.

items.title: Kazhdan's property (T)
items.statement: Let $G$ be a topological group. Then $G$ has Kazhdan’s property (T) if every strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) on a Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) that has almost invariant vectors ([[def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unitary-representation]]) has a nonzero $G$-invariant vector. Equivalently, whenever such a representation $(\pi,H)$ has, for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ ([[def-compact-space]]) and every $\varepsilon>0$, a unit vector $\xi$ satisfying $$\|\pi(x)\xi-\xi\|<\varepsilon\quad\text{for every }x\in Q.$$ Then $\pi$ has a nonzero vector fixed by every $\pi(g)$, $g\in G$.
items.strategy: Definition: the two displayed formulations are identical by the definition of almost invariant vectors and the definition of nonzero invariant vectors. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Almost invariant vectors and normalized positive type functions
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a topological group and $(\pi,H)$ a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]], [[def-hilbert-space]]). Then $\pi$ has almost invariant vectors ([[def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unitary-representation]]) if and only if there is a net $(\xi_i)_{i\in I}$, indexed by a directed set ([[def-directed-set-and-net]]), of unit vectors in $H$ whose normalized positive type coefficient functions $\varphi_i(g):=\langle\pi(g)\xi_i,\xi_i\rangle$ ([[def-matrix-coefficient-of-a-unitary-representation]], [[def-continuous-function-of-positive-type]]) converge to $1$ uniformly on compact subsets. Here this uniform convergence means that for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\eta>0$ there is $i_0\in I$ such that $|\varphi_i(x)-1|<\eta$ for all $i\ge i_0$ and all $x\in Q$. More generally, if a net, indexed by a directed set, of unit vectors in $H$ is eventually $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant for every compact $Q$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, then its coefficient net converges to $1$ uniformly on compact subsets. If $(\varphi_i)_{i\in I}$ is a net, indexed by a directed set, of normalized continuous positive type functions ([[def-continuous-function-of-positive-type]]) converging to $1$ uniformly on compact subsets, let $(\pi_{\varphi_i},H_{\varphi_i},\xi_{\varphi_i})$ be their GNS triples ([[thm-gns-construction-for-topological-groups]]). Then the cyclic vectors $\xi_{\varphi_i}$ are eventually $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant for every compact $Q$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, and the Hilbert direct sum $\widehat{\bigoplus}_{i\in I}\pi_{\varphi_i}$ ([[def-hilbert-direct-sum-of-unitary-representations]]) has almost invariant vectors. No claim is made that an individual $\pi_{\varphi_i}$ has almost invariant vectors.
items.strategy: Use the displacement/coefficient inequalities, an AC-selected net of witnesses, and the GNS direct sum; the converse is choice-free once a coefficient net is given.

items.title: Property (T) is equivalent to the existence of a compact Kazhdan pair
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group. The following are equivalent: (i) $G$ has property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]); (ii) $G$ has a compact Kazhdan set, that is, there are a compact $Q\subseteq G$ and an $\varepsilon>0$ such that $(Q,\varepsilon)$ is a Kazhdan pair ([[def-kazhdan-pair-and-kazhdan-constant]]); (iii) there is a compact $Q\subseteq G$ with $\kappa(G,Q)>0$. Moreover, if $(Q,\varepsilon)$ is a Kazhdan pair, $\pi$ is any unitary representation of $G$ and $\xi\in H$ is $(Q,\delta\varepsilon)$-invariant for some $0<\delta\le1$, then $\lVert\xi-P\xi\rVert\le\delta\lVert\xi\rVert$, where $P$ is the orthogonal projection of $H$ onto the closed subspace $H^G$ of $G$-invariant vectors.
items.strategy: (ii) implies (i) by the definitions. For (i) implies (ii), if no compact Kazhdan pair exists, define for each compact Q and eta>0 the nonempty subset C_(Q,eta) of C(G) consisting of normalized diagonal coefficients witnessing failure. AC selects one function from each set, and its canonical GNS representation has no invariant vectors by pointed cyclic uniqueness. The Hilbert direct sum then has almost invariant vectors but no invariant vector, contradicting (i). The definition of kappa gives (ii) iff (iii). For the quantitative clause, decompose xi into H^G and its orthogonal complement; a nonzero complementary component has a Q-displacement at least epsilon times its norm, while the assumed vector has displacement strictly below delta epsilon times its norm. If Q is empty, the pair forces the complement to vanish.

items.title: Property (T) and isolation of the trivial representation in the Fell dual
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), and let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group ([[def-topological-group]], [[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Then $G$ has Kazhdan's property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]) if and only if the class $[1_G]$ of the trivial representation $1_G(g)=I_{\mathbb C}$ is isolated in the Fell topology on the unitary dual $\widehat G$ ([[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-locally-compact-group]]). Equivalently, $G$ has property (T) if and only if for every set $R$ of unitary equivalence classes of strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) with $\widehat G\subseteq R$, such that every class in $R\setminus\{[1_G]\}$ has no nonzero invariant vector, $[1_G]$ is isolated in $R$.
items.strategy: T implies dual isolation by the exact Fell closure/weak-containment supplier and the single almost-invariant-vector lemma. For the converse, set I to the intersection of nontrivial irreducible C*(G)-kernels. Isolation makes I nontrivial at the trivial character; the in-run arbitrary C*-algebra separation lemma shows I intersects ker chi trivially, giving a central projection p with ap=pa=chi(a)p. If rho has almost invariant vectors, weak containment and kernel inclusion force pi(p) nonzero in its C*(G) representation. Prove its Hilbert projection decomposition directly, show both restrictions are nondegenerate, and use the group/C* correspondence to identify the nonzero range with a trivial-representation summand. The general R formulation is proved from actual finite-sum Fell neighborhoods and the published weak-containment-to-single-almost-invariant-vector lemma, never by applying dual closure to reducible classes.

items.title: Compactly generated locally compact groups
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group ([[def-topological-group]], [[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). It is **compactly generated** if some compact subset $K\subseteq G$ ([[def-compact-space]]) generates $G$ as an abstract group, that is, $\langle K\rangle=G$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]). Equivalently, there is a compact subset $Q\subseteq G$ with $e\in Q$ and $Q=Q^{-1}$ such that $$G=\bigcup_{n\ge1}Q^n,\qquad Q^n=\{q_1\cdots q_n:q_1,\ldots,q_n\in Q\}.$$ For the equivalence, given a compact generating set $K$, take $Q=K\cup K^{-1}\cup\{e\}$. Inversion is a homeomorphism, so $K^{-1}$ is compact; a finite union of compact subsets is compact by the open-cover definition. The set $Q$ is symmetric and contains $e$. Its positive finite products form a subgroup: they contain $e$, are closed under concatenation, and are closed under inverses by symmetry. This subgroup contains $K$ and is contained in every subgroup containing $K$, so it is exactly $\langle K\rangle$; the copies of $e$ pad shorter words to any larger exponent. Conversely, if a symmetric identity-containing $Q$ has $G=\bigcup_{n\ge1}Q^n$, then every element of $G$ belongs to the subgroup generated by $Q$. Every compact group is compactly generated, by taking $K=G$. More generally, every connected locally compact Hausdorff group is compactly generated, so in particular this holds for the connected $\sigma$-compact case. Indeed, choose a compact neighbourhood $K$ of the identity ([[def-neighbourhood-top]]) and let $H=\langle K\rangle$. Since $K$ contains an open neighbourhood $U$ of the identity, $H$ contains $U$ and is open: for each $h\in H$, the open set $hU$ lies in $H$. Every coset of an open subgroup is open, so the complement of $H$ is open as well. Thus $H$ is clopen, and connectedness forces $H=G$ ([[def-connected-space]]). No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Definition by a compact generating subset, equivalent to the positive-power exhaustion for a compact symmetric identity-containing set. The equivalence is proved by symmetrizing K and observing that finite products of the symmetric set give exactly its generated subgroup. A compact group is generated by itself. In a connected LCH group, a compact identity neighbourhood generates an open subgroup; the subgroup is also closed, hence is all of G by connectedness. All arguments are choice-free.

items.title: Quasi-regular representations on discrete coset spaces
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a topological group and let $H\le G$ be an open subgroup ([[def-subgroup]]). Give the left coset set $X=G/H:=\{gH:g\in G\}$ its quotient topology. Then $X$ is discrete, and $\ell^2(X):=\widehat{\bigoplus}_{xH\in X}\mathbb C$ is a Hilbert space whose norm is the counting-measure norm ([[def-hilbert-direct-sum-of-unitary-representations]], [[def-counting-measure]]). The left quasi-regular representation $$\lambda_{G/H}(g)f(xH):=f(g^{-1}xH)$$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]). Its Dirac vector $\delta_H$ at the identity coset is a unit vector fixed by $H$. The $G$-invariant vectors in $\ell^2(G/H)$ are exactly the constant functions; therefore this invariant subspace is nonzero if and only if $G/H$ is finite.
items.strategy: Give G/H its quotient topology; openness of H makes every coset open and the quotient discrete. Under AC, realize ell^2(G/H) as the Hilbert direct sum of one-dimensional coordinate spaces. Left translation permutes the coordinate basis, hence is unitary. Open conjugate stabilizers make basis-vector orbit maps locally constant, and finite-support density extends continuity to all vectors. Invariance forces coordinates to be constant; a nonzero constant vector is square-summable exactly when G/H is finite. The identity-coset Dirac vector is unit and H-fixed.

items.title: Property (T) implies compact generation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group ([[def-topological-group]], [[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]) with Kazhdan's property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]). Then $G$ is compactly generated ([[def-compactly-generated-locally-compact-group]]). In particular, a discrete group with property (T) is finitely generated.
items.strategy: Assume G is not compactly generated and form the set C of all open compactly generated subgroups. Local compactness gives compact neighborhoods whose generated subgroups are open, so C covers G; compactness then puts each compact Q inside one H0 in C by taking the subgroup generated by finitely many compact generators. Every G/H is infinite under the contradiction hypothesis. The strongly continuous Hilbert direct sum of the quasi-regular representations has no invariant vector, while the single-coordinate Dirac vector in H0 is fixed by Q, so it has almost invariant vectors. Property (T) yields a nonzero invariant coordinate, forcing finite index and hence compact generation, a contradiction. The discrete case follows because compact subsets of a discrete space are finite.

items.title: Property (T) passes to Hausdorff quotients
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group with property (T), and let $N\trianglelefteq G$ be a closed normal subgroup. Then the Hausdorff quotient topological group $G/N$ with the quotient topology has property (T).
items.strategy: Let q:G→G/N. Verify q is open and that the closed normal quotient is a Hausdorff topological group, with multiplication descended through the open quotient map q×q. For any strongly continuous representation σ of G/N with almost invariant vectors, π=σ∘q is strongly continuous. Every compact K⊂G has compact image q(K), so almost invariant vectors pull back to π; property (T) of G gives a nonzero invariant vector, and surjectivity of q makes it G/N-invariant. Thus G/N has property (T). No AC is used by the proof.

The source proves the stronger result for a continuous homomorphism with dense image; this item retains the dispatched closed-normal quotient claim and proves it directly by pulling representations back along the quotient map.

items.title: Spectral gap for a unitary representation
items.statement: Let $G$ be a topological group and let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) on a Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Put $$H^G:=\{\xi\in H:\pi(g)\xi=\xi\text{ for every }g\in G\}.$$ This is a closed invariant subspace: if $\xi_n\in H^G$ and $\xi_n\to\xi$, then for every $g$ the isometry $\pi(g)$ gives $\|\pi(g)\xi-\xi\|\le2\|\xi-\xi_n\|\to0$. Its orthogonal complement $H^G{}^\perp$ ([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) is also closed and $G$-invariant by [[lem-unitary-invariant-subspaces-have-invariant-orthogonal-complements]], so the restriction $\pi|_{H^G{}^\perp}$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation. The representation $\pi$ has **spectral gap** if $$1_G\not\prec\pi|_{H^G{}^\perp},$$ where $1_G$ is the trivial representation and $\prec$ is weak containment ([[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]]). If $G$ is locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]) and AC is assumed ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), this is equivalent by [[lem-weak-containment-of-the-trivial-representation-and-almost-invariant-vectors]] to the existence of a compact $Q\subseteq G$ containing the identity and an $\varepsilon>0$ such that $$\sup_{g\in Q}\|\pi(g)\xi-\xi\|\ge\varepsilon\|\xi\|\qquad\text{for every }\xi\in H^G{}^\perp.$$ No displacement equivalence is asserted for general topological groups. The weak-containment lemma says, under its LCH and AC hypotheses, that $1_G\prec\pi|_{H^G{}^\perp}$ exactly when every compact $Q$ and every $\delta>0$ admit a unit vector in $H^G{}^\perp$ with displacement $<\delta$. Negating this statement gives one compact $Q$ and one $\varepsilon>0$ for which every unit vector has displacement at least $\varepsilon$. Rescaling gives the displayed bound for every nonzero vector, and for $\xi=0$ both sides are zero. Replacing $Q$ by $Q\cup\{e\}$ preserves the bound and ensures the compact set is nonempty. If $H^G{}^\perp=\{0\}$, the weak-containment condition fails and the displacement inequality holds vacuously apart from its true zero-vector equality.
items.strategy: Define spectral gap as non-weak-containment of the trivial representation in the restriction to the invariant orthogonal complement. Prove the fixed-vector subspace is closed directly and use the choice-free invariant-orthogonal-complement lemma. Under LCH and AC, negate the published almost-invariant-vector equivalence, normalize nonzero vectors, handle zero vectors, and enlarge the compact set to contain the identity. No projection or orthogonal-decomposition existence theorem is used.

items.axiom_audit: The invariant-vector subspace, its orthogonal complement, and the weak-containment definition are choice-free. The displacement characterization is invoked only for LCH groups under the explicit Axiom of Choice hypothesis of the published weak-containment lemma. No countable-choice projection or orthogonal-decomposition result is used.

items.title: Property (T) is a uniform spectral gap over all representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group. Then $G$ has property (T) if and only if there are a compact $Q\subseteq G$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that for every strongly continuous unitary representation $(\pi,H)$ and every $\xi\in(H^G)^\perp$, $\sup_{x\in Q}\lVert\pi(x)\xi-\xi\rVert\ge\varepsilon\lVert\xi\rVert$, with the empty-$Q$ supremum defined to be $0$. In the property-(T) direction $Q$ may be chosen to contain the identity; any uniform pair is a Kazhdan pair. For locally compact Hausdorff $G$, this is equivalent to one compact set and constant witnessing spectral gap for every unitary representation simultaneously.
items.strategy: Property (T) and the in-run Kazhdan-pair equivalence supply a compact pair; adjoin the identity so Q is nonempty. On any representation, restrict to (H^G)^perp; it has no nonzero invariant vector, so a unit vector there cannot be (Q,eps)-invariant, giving the uniform displacement lower bound. Conversely, for a (Q,eps)-invariant unit vector xi, decompose xi=Pxi+xi″. Uniform gap applied to xi″ shows its norm is <1: if Q is nonempty, compactness makes the strict pointwise displacement attain a maximum below eps, while if Q is empty the uniform bound forces xi″=0. Pythagoras makes Pxi nonzero, so (Q,eps) is a Kazhdan pair and G has property (T). For LCH groups, the spectral-gap definition identifies the common displacement bound with spectral gap for each representation. AC supplies the pair-equivalence theorem and implies Countable Choice for the projection suppliers.

AC implies Countable Choice through the declared theorem, which the projection and orthogonal-decomposition suppliers require in the converse. No further choice is used.

items.title: Compactness, finite Haar volume and invariant vectors in the regular representation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group ([[def-topological-group]], [[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]) with a left Haar measure $\mu$ ([[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]]) and the left regular representation $\lambda_G$ on $L^2(G)$ ([[def-left-and-right-regular-unitary-representations]], [[thm-regular-representations-are-unitary-and-strongly-continuous]], [[def-complex-haar-lp-spaces-and-compactly-supported-functions]]). Then the following are equivalent: 1. $G$ is compact. 2. $\mu(G)<\infty$. 3. $\lambda_G$ has a nonzero invariant vector. 4. The constant function $1$ belongs to $L^2(G)$. Moreover, $\mu(G)>0$ always. Thus, when $G$ is compact, $\mu/\mu(G)$ is a left Haar probability measure.
items.strategy: Compact G gives finite Haar measure. Finite Haar measure is equivalent to the constant 1 being in L2, and positivity of Haar measure makes that vector nonzero and invariant. Conversely, approximate a nonzero invariant L2 vector by a compactly supported continuous function to find a compact set K carrying positive mass. In a noncompact group, AC selects a sequence of pairwise disjoint translates of K; invariance gives each translate the same positive L2 mass, contradicting finiteness. AC is the exact global choice assumption for the regular-representation and L2-density suppliers and for the selector over finite histories.

items.title: An amenable locally compact group with property (T) is compact
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). If $G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]) and has property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]), then $G$ is compact. Equivalently, no non-compact locally compact group can be both amenable and a Kazhdan group.
items.strategy: By the Hulanicki criterion ([[thm-hulanicki-weak-containment-criterion-for-amenability]]) amenability of $G$ is equivalent to $1_G\prec\lambda_G$, equivalently ([[lem-weak-containment-of-the-trivial-representation-and-almost-invariant-vectors]]) to $\lambda_G$ having almost invariant vectors. Property (T) then produces a nonzero invariant vector of the left regular representation, and [[lem-finite-haar-volume-compactness-criterion]] forces $G$ to be compact. This is the precise content of Bekka-de la Harpe-Valette Theorem 1.1.6. AC is inherited from the Hulanicki criterion and the Haar measure suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

references.locator: Chapter 1, Theorem 1.1.6 and complete proof, printed p. 35/PDF p. 41: amenability gives almost invariant vectors for the left regular representation; property (T) gives a nonzero invariant vector; Remark 1.1.2(vii) then gives compactness.

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC. It is inherited from the Hulanicki-Reiter and weak-containment-to-almost-invariant-vector suppliers and the finite-Haar-volume criterion. No additional choice is used.

items.title: Compact groups have property (T) by Haar averaging
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group with normalized Haar probability measure $\mu$. Then $(K,\varepsilon)$ is a Kazhdan pair for every $0<\varepsilon\le1$; in particular, $K$ is a Kazhdan set and has property (T). Explicitly, if $(\pi,H)$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation and $\xi\in H$ is a unit vector with $\sup_{x\in K}\lVert\pi(x)\xi-\xi\rVert<1$, the Bochner average $\eta:=\int_K\pi(x)\xi\,d\mu(x)$ is a nonzero $K$-invariant vector and $\lVert\eta-\xi\rVert\le\sup_{x\in K}\lVert\pi(x)\xi-\xi\rVert.$
items.strategy: For a unit vector xi, the continuous orbit map x↦pi(x)xi on compact K admits finite-valued Borel simple approximants uniformly within 1/n; AC selects a finite cover and sample points for each n, and AC also supplies normalized Haar probability. The Bochner average eta is within the maximum K-displacement of xi by estimating the finite simple integrals. Left invariance of Haar measure, checked first on these simple approximants and then by uniform limits, makes eta K-invariant. If xi is (K,epsilon)-invariant with 0<epsilon<=1, compactness makes its maximum displacement strictly below epsilon, so eta is nonzero and (K,epsilon) is a Kazhdan pair. Taking epsilon=1 and using the definition of property (T) proves the remaining claims. The source instead gives the stronger (G,sqrt(2)) pair by a closed-convex-hull argument; this item proves the Haar-average route locally.

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC. It is used for the normalized Haar probability and to choose, for each n, a finite subcover together with sample points, forming a sequence of Bochner simple approximants. Compactness gives each finite subcover and finite choice supplies its sample points. The averaging and invariance arguments make no further choice.

items.title: Relative property (T) for a pair and relative Kazhdan pairs
items.statement: Let $G$ be a topological group and let $H\le G$ be any subgroup ([[def-subgroup]]), not assumed normal or closed. The pair $(G,H)$ has relative property (T) if every strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) with almost invariant vectors ([[def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unitary-representation]]) has a nonzero vector fixed by every $\pi(h)$ for $h\in H$. A pair $(Q,\varepsilon)$ with $Q\subseteq G$ and $\varepsilon>0$ is a relative Kazhdan pair for $(G,H)$ if every strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ having a $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant unit vector has a nonzero $H$-invariant vector. A subset $Q\subseteq G$ is a relative Kazhdan set if $(Q,\varepsilon)$ is a relative Kazhdan pair for some $\varepsilon>0$. When $H=G$, these are respectively Kazhdan’s property (T), Kazhdan pairs, and Kazhdan sets ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]], [[def-kazhdan-pair-and-kazhdan-constant]]).
items.strategy: Definition; H=G reduces to property (T) by the definitions, and no choice principle is used.

Define SL2(R) in R^4, prove its group and topological-group properties by determinant and coordinate formulas, and prove joint action continuity in the t and reciprocal s charts. items.title: No invariant projective-line probability for two unipotents with distinct fixed lines
items.statement: Let $P^1(\mathbb R)$ be the real projective line with the natural action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-real-projective-line-and-its-sl2-action]]). Let $u_1,u_2\in\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ be unipotent matrices, meaning $u_i\ne I$ and $(u_i-I)^2=0$, whose fixed lines in $\mathbb R^2$ are distinct. There is no Borel probability measure on $P^1(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]], [[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]) invariant under both $u_1$ and $u_2$, where invariance means $\mu(u_i A)=\mu(A)$ for every Borel set $A$. In particular, no Borel probability measure is invariant under both $u_+=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $u_-=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.
items.strategy: Choose nonzero vectors on the two distinct fixed lines and rescale the second so the basis matrix S has determinant 1. Conjugation by S puts the unipotents in the forms I+cE_12 and I+c'E_21 with c,c' nonzero. Push the assumed probability forward by S^{-1}; the resulting measure remains invariant under both conjugates. The first acts on finite t=x/y by t↦t+c and fixes infinity. Let d=|c|>0; the Borel intervals [kd,(k+1)d), k∈Z, partition R and are permuted by translation by c, including when c<0. Invariance makes all their masses equal; finite total mass forces each to be zero, and countable additivity gives zero mass to R, so the measure is the Dirac mass at infinity. The second unipotent sends infinity to [1:c'] in the finite chart, contradicting invariance. The proof is choice-free and the one-unipotent case is degenerate because its fixed-point Dirac measure is invariant.

items.title: Relative property (T) for SL2(R) semidirect R2
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $K=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ with its matrix subspace topology and let $V=\mathbb R^2$ with its usual additive topology. Write $G=K\ltimes V$ for the group on $K\times V$ with product topology and multiplication $(k,v)(k',v')=(kk',v+k v')$; this is the coordinate-swapped form of the external semidirect product ([[def-external-semidirect-product]], [[thm-external-semidirect-product-is-a-group]]). Let $N=\{(I,v):v\in V\}$ be the translation subgroup. Put $u_+=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $u_-=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, and $Q_0=\{(u_+,0),(u_+^{-1},0),(u_-,0),(u_-^{-1},0)\}$. Then there is $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$ such that every strongly continuous unitary representation $(\pi,H)$ of $G$ having a $(Q_0,\varepsilon_0)$-invariant unit vector ([[def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unitary-representation]]) has a nonzero $N$-invariant vector. In particular, $(G,N)$ has relative property (T) ([[def-relative-property-t-for-a-pair]]).
items.strategy: Assume no finite four-element relative Kazhdan pair works and, using AC on the set of coefficient functions in C^G, choose normalized counterexample coefficients indexed by m. Form canonical GNS cyclic representations; locally prove the coefficient-preserving isometries onto witness cyclic carriers, and use second countability to obtain separable Hilbert spaces. Apply the covariant spectral-measure lemma for R^2 ⋊ SL2(R), prove the real dual homeomorphism in compact-open topology, and identify N-invariant vectors with the zero spectral fiber using the dense countable subgroup Q^2. The absence of N-invariants makes the spectral probabilities atomless at zero; push them to P^1(R), use the coefficient displacement bound to get a 2/m discrepancy on every Borel set under the two dual unipotents, and pass to a weak limit using finite-valued continuous-test approximations. The limit is invariant under two nonidentity unipotents with distinct fixed lines, contradicting the projective-line lemma. Therefore some epsilon=1/m gives the claimed relative Kazhdan pair; finite Q_0 makes it imply relative property (T).

items.title: Normal relative property (T) controls the distance to the invariant subspace
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a topological group, let $N\trianglelefteq G$ be a closed normal subgroup ([[def-normal-subgroup]]), and let $(Q,\varepsilon)$ be a relative Kazhdan pair for $(G,N)$ ([[def-relative-property-t-for-a-pair]]). For a strongly continuous unitary representation $(\pi,H)$ and $\xi\in H$, put $H^N:=\{v\in H:\pi(n)v=v\text{ for every }n\in N\}$ and define $\Delta_Q^\pi(\xi):=0$ if $Q=\varnothing$, while for nonempty $Q$ set $\Delta_Q^\pi(\xi):=\sup_{q\in Q}\|\pi(q)\xi-\xi\|$. This supremum exists in $\mathbb R$ because each displacement is at most $2\|\xi\|$. Then $$\operatorname{dist}(\xi,H^N)\le\varepsilon^{-1}\Delta_Q^\pi(\xi),\qquad\sup_{n\in N}\|\pi(n)\xi-\xi\|\le2\varepsilon^{-1}\Delta_Q^\pi(\xi),$$ where $\operatorname{dist}(\xi,H^N):=\inf_{v\in H^N}\|\xi-v\|$. Moreover, if $(G,N)$ has relative property (T), then for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ with $\bigcup_{k\ge1}Q^k=G$, where $Q^k$ is the set of products of $k$ elements of $Q$, there is $\delta>0$ such that every strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ without a nonzero $N$-invariant vector satisfies $\Delta_Q^\pi(\xi)\ge\delta\|\xi\|$ for every $\xi\in H$.
items.strategy: Assume relative property (T) but no compact relative Kazhdan pair. For each compact K and positive integer m, the failed pair (K,1/m) gives a representation without N-invariants and a unit (K,1/m)-invariant vector. Its coefficient belongs to a nonempty set F_{K,m} of functions G→C. These are sets indexed by the set of compact subsets of G and the positive integers, so AC selects one function per index without choosing from a proper class of representations. GNS uniqueness gives a canonical cyclic N-free representation and unit vector for each selected function; their AC-dependent Hilbert direct sum has almost invariant vectors, contradicting relative (T). Hence there is a compact relative Kazhdan pair (K0,eps0). For an arbitrary pair (Q,eps), H^N is a closed G-invariant subspace because N is normal; decompose H=H^N⊕(H^N)^perp using AC⇒Countable Choice. The complement has no nonzero N-invariants, so the relative pair gives a displacement at least eps times the complement norm. Pythagoras yields the distance estimate and the bound on all N-displacements. For the final uniform-gap clause, choose normalized positive-type coefficients with Q-displacements tending to zero from sets of functions, transfer N-free witnesses to canonical GNS, and telescope words to obtain pointwise convergence to 1. The compact image of K0 in the countable product of complex coefficient values is Hausdorff. The complex C0 dual representation and dominated convergence against finite variation give weak convergence in C(X). Mazur supplies a finite convex combination uniformly close to 1; the weighted finite direct sum is N-free but has a (K0,eps0)-invariant unit vector, a contradiction. No additional hypothesis on G or Q is imposed.

items.title: Bounded elementary generation of SLn(R) by transvections
items.statement: Let $n\ge2$. For $1\le i\ne j\le n$, let $e_{ij}$ be the standard matrix unit and put $E_{ij}(t):=I_n+t e_{ij}$ for $t\in\mathbb R$, the elementary transvection ([[def-elementary-matrix]], [[def-elementary-row-operations-and-row-equivalence]], [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]). Define $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R):=\{g\in M_n(\mathbb R):\det g=1\}$ using the determinant ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]). Then every $g\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ is a product of at most $M(n):=2n^2+6n$ elementary transvections $E_{ij}(t)$ (factors $E_{ij}(0)=I_n$ are allowed). In particular, $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ is boundedly generated by its elementary root subgroups $H_{ij}:=\{E_{ij}(t):t\in\mathbb R\}.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every integer $n\ge3$, the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ with its embedded matrix Lie group topology has Kazhdan's property (T).
items.strategy: For each ordered triple (i,j,k) with i≠j and k distinct, embed a topological copy of SL2(R)⋉R² in SLn(R), with Eij(t) contained in its translation subgroup. The relative-(T) supplier gives the same finite relative Kazhdan pair in every copy. Let Q* be the finite union of their test sets and set ε=δ/(4M(n)), where M(n) bounds real transvection generation. For a (Q*,ε)-invariant unit vector, the second inequality from the normal-relative supplier bounds displacement under every translation by 1/(2M); bounded generation and telescoping put the entire orbit in the radius-1/2 ball about ξ. The closed convex hull is G-invariant and contained in that ball. Under AC→CC its unique least-norm point exists, lies within 1/2 of ξ and is nonzero; invariance and uniqueness make it G-fixed. Thus Q* is a compact Kazhdan pair and SLn(R) has property (T). The consumer uses the supplier's second quantitative inequality at F3/Proof 3.1.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The group $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ does not have property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]). Explicitly, for every compact $Q\subseteq\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $

u}$ ([[def-normalized-principal-series-i-epsilon-nu]], [[thm-unitarity-of-the-sl2-complementary-series]]) has no nonzero invariant vector but has a $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant unit vector ([[def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unitary-representation]]), namely its $K$-fixed vector $f_0$ for $
u$ sufficiently close to $1$. Consequently no pair $(Q,\varepsilon)$ with $Q$ compact is a Kazhdan pair ([[def-kazhdan-pair-and-kazhdan-constant]]).
items.strategy: The positive complementary weights make every smooth even K-mode a nonzero vector in the weighted Hilbert completion with its original right-K character. Irreducibility then excludes invariant vectors. Compact-uniform coefficient convergence gives (Q,epsilon)-invariant f0 vectors and parameter-family Fell convergence; the explicit cofinal-parameter direct sum supplies one representation with almost invariant vectors and no fixed vector. All uses are under the declared AC, and no ordinary-L2 norm is transferred to the complementary completion.

items.title: A Kazhdan pair for a compact group via Haar averaging
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group ([[def-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-group]]) with normalized Haar probability measure $\mu$ ([[cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group]]). For every $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $(K,\varepsilon)$ is a Kazhdan pair ([[def-kazhdan-pair-and-kazhdan-constant]]); in particular, $K$ is a Kazhdan set and has property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]). Explicitly, if $(\pi,H)$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) on a Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and $\xi\in H$ is a unit vector with $$\sup_{x\in K}\lVert\pi(x)\xi-\xi\rVert<\varepsilon\le1,$$ then its Haar average $\eta=\int_K\pi(x)\xi\,d\mu(x)$, as in [[thm-compact-groups-have-property-t]], is nonzero and $K$-invariant, with $$\lVert\eta-\xi\rVert\le\sup_{x\in K}\lVert\pi(x)\xi-\xi\rVert.$$ Thus the whole group $K$ is a Kazhdan set with tolerance $1$; the averaging bound is not claimed to be optimal.
items.strategy: Apply the earlier compact-groups Haar-average theorem directly. Its all-epsilon Kazhdan-pair conclusion gives (K,epsilon) for 0<epsilon<=1; its explicit estimate applies because sup<epsilon<=1 implies sup<1, giving the nonzero invariant average and displacement bound. Set epsilon=1 for the compact Kazhdan set and property-(T) endpoint.

items.title: Property (T) for finite groups via normalized counting measure
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group ([[def-group]]) with the discrete topology ([[def-standard-topologies]]) and let $m:=|\Gamma|$. Its normalized counting measure $\mu(A):=|A|/m$ ([[def-counting-measure]], [[prop-counting-measure-is-a-measure]]) is its Haar probability measure ([[cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group]]). Every $(\Gamma,\varepsilon)$ is a Kazhdan pair ([[def-kazhdan-pair-and-kazhdan-constant]]) for $0<\varepsilon\le1$, so $\Gamma$ has property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]). For every strongly continuous unitary representation ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) $\pi$ on a Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), the finite average $$P\xi:=\frac1m\sum_{g\in\Gamma}\pi(g)\xi$$ is the orthogonal projection ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) onto the closed linear subspace ([[def-linear-subspace]]) $$H^\Gamma:=\{\zeta\in H:\pi(g)\zeta=\zeta\text{ for every }g\in\Gamma\},$$ and in particular $\|P\xi\|\le\|\xi\|$.
items.strategy: A finite discrete group is compact Hausdorff and locally compact. Verify directly that normalized counting measure is a Radon left-invariant probability, so uniqueness identifies it with normalized Haar measure; apply the completed A-page compact-group theorem for every Kazhdan pair and property (T). Define the finite average P, reindex left multiplication to show its image is invariant and it fixes invariant vectors, then use unitarity to show xi-Pxi is orthogonal to the invariant subspace. AC implies Countable Choice for the Hilbert projection interface; the projection lemma supplies contractivity. No B-page supplier is used.

items.title: The integers do not have property (T)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), and give the additive group $\mathbb Z$ ([[def-integers]]) the discrete topology ([[def-standard-topologies]]). For every compact subset $Q\subseteq\mathbb Z$ ([[def-compact-space]]) and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a complex number $z$ with $|z|=1$ and $z\ne1$ such that the character $\chi_z(n)=z^n$ defines a strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi_z(n)u=z^n u$ on the standard complex Hilbert space $\mathbb C$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) with no nonzero invariant vector, while its unit vector $1$ is $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant ([[def-almost-invariant-vectors-for-a-unitary-representation]]): $$|z^n-1|<\varepsilon\qquad(n\in Q).$$ Consequently, no compact subset of $\mathbb Z$ is a Kazhdan set, and $\mathbb Z$ does not have property (T) ([[def-kazhdans-property-t]]) by [[thm-property-t-is-equivalent-to-the-existence-of-a-kazhdan-pair]]. No compact Kazhdan pair exists ([[def-kazhdan-pair-and-kazhdan-constant]]).
items.strategy: For a compact test set in the discrete group Z, use the explicit scalar z_t=((1-t^2)+2it)/(1+t^2), whose powers stay uniformly close to 1 when t is chosen from the finite maximum of the tested integer exponents. The corresponding one-dimensional character has no invariant vector whenever z_t is nontrivial. Apply the AC-dependent compact Kazhdan pair characterization only for the final property-(T) implication.

items.title: The spherical complementary series destroys property (T) for SL2(R)
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For $0<

u}$ is $(Q,\varepsilon)$-invariant for $
u$ close enough to $1$, while $I_{0,
u}$ has no nonzero invariant vector.
